Fixed model choices of an R-squared budget prior

Source: R/priors-R2.R
R2_model.Rd

R2_model() declares the fixed choices of a prior_R2() budget: the coefficient law, how a model of a model space derives its prior from the full candidate model, the residual scale, and the factor contrast. These are fixed model choices, not parameters with prior distributions; one specification can serve several budgets.

R2_model(
  law = "exact",
  convention = "common",
  concentration = "inherited",
  sigma = "sigma",
  contrast = "orthonormal"
)

check_R2_model(model, name = "model")

# S3 method for class 'R2_model'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

law

coefficient law: "exact" (default) allocates squared signal magnitudes exactly, with a fair sign for one-column terms and a uniform direction in the term's coefficient space (in the empirical design metric) for multi-column terms; "normal" is the normal kernel of the R2D2M2 prior and "laplace" the double-exponential kernel of the R2D2 prior, both allocating the budget over the individual coded coefficients, each with the concentration of its term.

convention

how a model derives the Beta shapes of its total from the total = Beta(a, b) of the full candidate model, with \(A\) the total concentration of the full model and \(A_M\) the total concentration retained by model \(M\): "common" (default) uses Beta(a, b) in every model; "linked" uses Beta(\(A_M\), b), so the first shape of total must equal \(A\); "conditioning" keeps \(a_M - A_M\) and \(a_M + b_M\) equal to \(a - A\) and \(a + b\).

concentration

concentrations of the retained units: "inherited" (default) keeps the concentrations of the allocation; "fixed_total" rescales them in every model to the sum of the concentrations of the allocation.

sigma

residual standard deviation that multiplies the coefficients, as the "multiply_by" attribute of a formula prior: the name of a parameter of the model (default "sigma") or a positive number.

contrast

contrast of the factor terms of the budget: "orthonormal" (default), "meandif", or "treatment"; used only when the budget contains a factor term.

model

an R-squared budget specification to validate.

name

argument name used in validation messages.

x

an R-squared budget specification.

...

additional arguments, currently unused.

Value

R2_model() returns an object of class "R2_model" with the five choices; check_R2_model() and print() return their validated input invisibly.

See also

prior_R2(), R2_dirichlet()

Examples

model <- R2_model(law = "normal", convention = "linked")
model
#> R-squared budget model
#>   law:           normal
#>   convention:    linked
#>   concentration: inherited
#>   sigma:         'sigma'
#>   contrast:      orthonormal (factor terms only)
# one specification for two budgets of a formula prior list
list(
  covariates = prior_R2(terms = c("age", "sex"), model = model,
                        total = prior("beta", list(2, 2))),
  tested     = prior_R2(terms = "treatment", model = model)
)
#> $covariates
#> R-squared budget prior (normal kernel (R2D2M2))
#>   terms:      age, sex
#>   total:      Beta(2, 2) in the full model; Beta(A_M, 2) in a model with retained concentration A_M
#>   allocation: Dirichlet(1, 1), retained terms keep their concentrations; each coded coefficient has its term's concentration
#>   scale:      coefficients in units of 'sigma'
#>   contrast:   orthonormal (factor terms only)
#> 
#> $tested
#> R-squared budget prior (normal kernel (R2D2M2))
#>   terms:      treatment
#>   total:      Beta(1, 1) in the full model; Beta(A_M, 1) in a model with retained concentration A_M
#>   allocation: concentration 1 of the single term (of each coded coefficient under the kernel laws)
#>   scale:      coefficients in units of 'sigma'
#>   contrast:   orthonormal (factor terms only)
#>
